title: Neutrality and current belong to a frame
question: How can a neutral current acquire charge density?
recap: Charge density and longitudinal current mix under a frame change. Zero charge density with nonzero current is allowed; it cannot be handled by dividing current by charge density to invent one charge velocity.
premises: Use a physical charge-current distribution and a boost along x.
Track the same isolated body when comparing its total charge.
limitations: Charge density is not total charge.
A neutral two-species current need not have a single common velocity.

overview.text: Charge density and longitudinal current mix under a frame change. Zero charge density with nonzero current is allowed; it cannot be handled by dividing current by charge density to invent one charge velocity.

full.spoken: Primed charge density is gamma times rho minus v J x over c squared; primed longitudinal current is gamma times J x minus v rho.

full.text: The transverse current components remain unchanged for this aligned boost. For \(\rho = 0\) and \(J_x\) nonzero, \(\rho'\) generally is not zero. The individual charged species must be transformed consistently rather than treating \(J/\rho\) as meaningful at neutrality.

Charge conservation requires density and current to satisfy the continuity equation together. The charge-and-current laboratory compares these quantities and the total charge of a specified body. Integrating the same body over each frame’s simultaneous slice preserves its total charge; arbitrary open spatial boxes are a different comparison.

full.returnCaption: Return to how can a neutral current acquire charge density.

items: Record both charge density and all current components.
Transform \(\rho\) and \(J_x\) as a coupled pair.
Keep \(J_y\) and \(J_z\) unchanged for the aligned boost.
Do not divide by rho when the original system is neutral.
Check continuity and the boundary of the same charge-carrying body before comparing total charge.

margin.text: The source’s convection-current discussion is not silently rewritten as a universal single-fluid formula. A modern four-current is a useful verification language, explicitly distinct from the historical presentation.
